text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key idea is using clear naming conventions for variables and functions, so their purpose is obvious at a glance. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time. When you return to your project months later, readable code saves you hours of confusion. In short, writing clean code is an investment that always pays off.
